recordDecisions.title: Group constructions cannot refute the Set Cover Conjecture, including tensor powers
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Pratt (STOC 2024, arXiv:2311.02774, Corollary 1.12) showed that if the Set Cover Conjecture holds, then for every k the asymptotic rank of the balanced tripartitioning tensor T_k is at least tau_k = 8^k * C(3k,k) * C(2k,k) / 27^k. A natural way to bound this rank, and Pratt's own route to rank at most 8^k/2, is a group construction: maps f1, f2, f3 from k-subsets of a 3k-set to a group G with f1(A) f2(B) f3(C) = 1 exactly when A, B, C are pairwise disjoint (a partition analogue of the Cohn-Umans triple product property). We formalise that no such construction, in any finite group, abelian or not, can refute the conjecture: |G| > tau_k for every k >= 2. The same holds for Strassen combinatorial degenerations of group tensors (border-rank constructions), via |G| >= C(3k, floor(3k/2)) > tau_k. The proof formalises a rigidity theorem: the triple products always factor through pairwise commuting elements, f1(A) f2(B) f3(C) = prod_i g_i^(m_i - 1) with m the multiplicity vector, so non-abelian groups give no advantage, unlike in the Cohn-Umans approach to matrix multiplication. It also formalises a lift lemma giving |G| >= 2^(3k-1), which shows Pratt's 8^k/2 is exactly optimal among group restrictions. Pratt's Corollary 1.12 and the passage from a group embedding to a rank bound are cited, not formalised. The bounds concern the group size needed by such constructions, not the rank of T_k itself. Joint constructions for tensor powers are covered: a degeneration of a group tensor onto T_k^(tensor m) needs |G| >= C(3k, floor(3k/2))^m > tau_k^m, so the induced asymptotic-rank bound |G|^(1/m) stays above tau_k.

recordDecisions.title: Deterministic factoring in time N^{o(1)}
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: A Lean 4 proof, against Mathlib, that one deterministic Turing machine computes the smallest prime factor Nat.minFac N of every natural number N in time N^{o(1)}: for every k >= 1 there is a constant C_k such that the same machine halts with the correct output within C_k * 2^(n/k) steps on every n-bit input. The machine model is Mathlib's Turing machine model TM2 (Turing.FinTM2 with Turing.TM2ComputableInTime), with numbers in binary (Computability.encodeNat) and every stack alphabet finite. The best previously published deterministic bounds known to the authors have exponent 1/5 (Harvey 2021; Harvey and Hittmeir 2022). The proof reduces finding the smallest prime factor to counting divisors with prescribed leading bits, expresses that count as the value of a network of local checks carrying out Schoenhage-Strassen multiplication, and evaluates it with a re-proved form of the counting engine of the 2026 3-SAT preprint by Claude (Anthropic). The Challenge also states, as a proposition only and without proof, a conjecture that factoring can be done in time exp(O(log N / sqrt(log log N))). The ideas and the Lean code were generated by AI; the authors audited the statement, not the proof.

recordDecisions.title: Finite uniform Bernoulli shifts with unequal base entropy
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: There exist a countable group G and a nontrivial finite alphabet A such that the ordinary left Bernoulli shifts on A and A times A, equipped with their uniform product probability measures, are equivariantly measure-preservingly isomorphic on invariant conull measurable sets. The inverse is measurable. The finite alphabets have different cardinalities and therefore different uniform base Shannon entropies. The algebraic existence input is supplied by the pinned OpenAI proofs. This formalization does not certify all-base collapse, finitary continuity, the integer coding inputs, or the manuscript's later corollaries.

recordDecisions.title: Weak and strong βη-normalization in pure type systems with βη-conversion
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: A Lean formalization of the Barendregt-Geuvers-Klop conjecture, "weak normalization implies strong normalization", for the pure type systems PTS_βη of Geuvers (Logics and Type Systems, 1993), whose conversion rule uses βη-conversion. For every PTS specification, with no functionality assumption, it proves two theorems about the legal terms of PTS_βη. If every legal term is weakly βη-normalizing, then every legal term is strongly βη-normalizing. If every legal term is weakly β-normalizing, then every legal term is strongly βη-normalizing. The proof adapts OpenAI's 2026 proof of the β case for PTS_β, whose Lean files are included. An η-step can delete a λ-annotation, so the proof works from a weaker hypothesis, that every legal term has a β-reduct with no β-redex outside its λ-domains. Conversion is handled through domain erasure, candidates are indexed by βη-normal forms of erased types, and observation values are made η-canonical.

recordDecisions.title: The critical Almost Stacked Hypothesis fails on a nine-vertex graph
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: In graph pebbling, a move removes two pebbles from a vertex and adds one to a neighbour; a configuration is stackable if moves can bring all pebbles onto one vertex and clearable if moves can leave exactly one pebble. The stacking (clearing) number of a connected (connected non-bipartite) graph is the least t >= 2 such that every configuration of t pebbles is stackable (clearable). The Almost Stacked Hypothesis, in its critical form, says that this number equals the least t0 >= 2 such that every almost stacked configuration (one vertex arbitrary, every other vertex at most one pebble) of every size at least t0 is stackable (clearable). We formalise a counterexample to both clauses: on the nine-vertex graph G9 (graph6 HCQTaXi) the stacking and clearing numbers are 15, the only non-stackable and non-clearable configurations of size 14 are (0,0,1,0,0,5,0,8,0) and its automorphic image, neither almost stacked, while every almost stacked configuration of size at least 14 is stackable and clearable. Hence neither clause holds for all finite connected (respectively connected non-bipartite) graphs. The finite facts are proved by kernel evaluation (decide +kernel) of a verified exact losing-layer checker on certificate data; general lemmas (clearable implies stackable; monotonicity above the order) are proved by hand.

recordDecisions.title: A Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for real powers: proof, equality cases and weighted forms
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: For a vector v with nonnegative entries and a real number p, write v^p for the vector of p-th powers of its entries. Johnston, Plosker, Torrance and Varona (arXiv:2507.10327, Conjecture 5.1) conjectured that ‖v^p‖ ‖w^p‖ - ⟨v^p, w^p⟩ ≤ ‖v‖^p ‖w‖^p - ⟨v, w⟩^p for every real p ≥ 2 and all vectors v, w in ℝⁿ with positive entries, with the Euclidean norm and inner product. They proved it for integer p and showed that it fails for 1 < p < 2. This formalization proves the conjecture for every real p ≥ 2 and all vectors with nonnegative entries. It also determines every case of equality: for p > 2 equality holds exactly when v and w are linearly dependent or each has at most one nonzero entry, and for p = 2 there is one further family supported on two coordinates. Finally, for positive coordinate weights ω used in every norm and inner product, the weighted inequality holds for all nonnegative vectors exactly when ω_i ω_j ≥ 1 for all i ≠ j, a condition that does not depend on p. The proof shows that a 2 × 2 entrywise-power defect matrix is positive semidefinite, using a double integral formula and the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for integrals. The conjecture and its equality cases were also proved, independently and concurrently, by Johnston and Sababheh (arXiv:2610.12063).

recordDecisions.title: Erdős Problem 699: every counterexample has n ≤ j²
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Erdős Problem 699 (Erdős and Szekeres 1978) asks whether for every 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n/2 there is a prime p ≥ i dividing gcd(C(n, i), C(n, j)). The problem is open. Using the statement from google-deepmind/formal-conjectures with the single extra hypothesis j² < n, this project proves in Lean 4 with Mathlib that the answer is yes whenever j² < n; equivalently, every counterexample (n, i, j) has n ≤ j². The proof combines the Erdős–Szekeres inequality gcd(C(n, i), C(n, j)) ≥ C(n, i)/C(j, i) ≥ (n/j)^i, which follows from the identity C(n, j) C(j, i) = C(n, i) C(n − i, j − i), with an upper bound for a gcd whose prime factors are all below i: each prime power in C(n, i) is at most n (Kummer), and there are at most i/2 primes below i, so such a gcd is at most n^(i/2). The bound reduces the problem to j ≥ √n. With a computer search of every n < 10^12 (not part of this formalization) it rules out counterexamples with j ≤ 10^6. The argument is short and may well be folklore; formal-conjectures records the problem but no partial result of this kind.

recordDecisions.title: BandParity: the band-parity sum of a quartic character, two laws modulo 4
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: For a prime p = 5 (mod 8) let chi be the quartic Dirichlet character with chi(2) = i, with values in the Gaussian integers, and let C(p) = f + i e be the sum of chi(n) (-1)^floor(n^2/p) over 0 < n < p/2. The development proves that f = (p-1)/4 (mod 4) and e = kappa (mod 4) for every such p, where kappa is the sum of the Legendre symbols (n/p) over 0 < n < p/4. The mechanism is a matching lemma: for sign functions sigma, tau and a bijection pi, the correlation sum sigma(x) tau(pi x) is congruent modulo 4 to the sum of the two marginals minus the number of terms, so it does not depend on pi. Along the way it proves the parity dictionary (-1)^floor(n^2/p) = s(n) s(n^2) with s(x) = (-1)^<x>, the coset form f = sum over the fourth powers H of s(u) s(u^2) and e = the same sum over 2H, the lag identity sum over 2H of s(u) s(2u) = kappa exactly, the exact coset parities sum_H s = k + 2t and sum_{2H} s = t - 2k where B_{1,chi} = k + i t, and the Coordinate Congruence kappa = (p-1)/4 + k + t (mod 4). It also proves the odd-subgroup congruence: for an odd modulus N >= 3, a subgroup H of (Z/N)^x of odd order h, a coset X = xH and an even exponent e >= 2, the band-parity sum of X and -X over (0, N/2) equals sum over X of s(u) s(u^e) and is congruent to h - 2 alpha(X) - 2 alpha(X^e) modulo 4, where alpha counts elements with odd least residue.

recordDecisions.title: Bounds for the iteration x ↦ a mod x
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: For integers 0 < b < a, let P(a,b) count the positive terms obtained by repeatedly replacing x by a mod x, starting at b. This development proves the uniform bound P(a,b) ≤ C_ε a^((41301 - 3 sqrt(82849))/137480 + ε) for every ε > 0, including the external coefficient-uniform affine-curve theorem and the effective Hilbert specialisation sieve, and its rational instance 4317/14677. It also proves the exterior-lattice exponents 471/1559 - 6 sqrt(105)/7795 and 153/520, the joint-invariant exponents (1310-sqrt(655))/4365, 2201/7480 and 128/435 and the earlier exponents 45/152, 8/27, 11/37, 23/77, and 3/10. It also proves a bound O(a^(1/4) sqrt R), where R minus one counts rises in the quotient increments, and positivity and integrality of the orbit's Hankel invariants. A separate conditional theorem gives O(a^(3/10) sqrt(log log(3a))) assuming two explicitly stated analytic estimates whose proofs are not formalised. The polar bound uses the proved orbit identity, actual common-base bound of four, degree-twelve residue labels, uniform arithmetic specialisation count, and full-pattern completion count with arbitrary common divisors. These establish the six-term local estimate without additional hypotheses. The conjectured O((log a)^2) bound remains open.

recordDecisions.title: Proofs and corrections of OEIS conjectures
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Machine-checked proofs of conjectures recorded in 29 entries of the On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences (OEIS), together with corrections of the four conjectured statements that turn out to be false. Most of the sequences are coefficients of formal power series defined by functional equations, and most of the results describe their residues modulo small integers. The results form six families and a group of further results: the equation A(x*A - m*x*A^2) = x^2 (parity, residues modulo m^2, binary-digit divisibility and prime exponents for every m, with corrected residue classifications modulo 9 and 16 for A396843 and A396844); consecutive iterates F = x + F^{o r}*F^{o(r+1)} (every integer iterate modulo 2r, A396099, A396798, A396807); scaled inverses A(x - x*A(qx)/q) = x (every coefficient is 1 modulo q+1, and for even q the odd coefficients are exactly at the powers of 2, A393856-A393859); theta-series substitutions and theta-type sums (square patterns modulo 4, corrected for A380680, and a congruence modulo 16 for A355872); Catalan-type equations (residues modulo 2, 4 and 8 governed by powers of 2, A393172, A393171, A389536, A397588, A195194); equations with an exact halving step (residues modulo 4, 9 and 3, A389537, A389542, A389474, A389475); and further results on A396093, A392210, A396102 and its family F^{o r} = (1+x)*F^{o(r-1)}, A380056, A397346 and the greedy sequence A394576. Each family has its own Comparator configuration, and each OEIS entry has a self-contained paper in the repository.

recordDecisions.title: The Art Gallery Problem is ∃ℝ-complete: point-point, boundary-point and point-boundary variants, in Lean 4
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of Abrahamsen, Adamaszek and Miltzow, "The Art Gallery Problem is ∃ℝ-complete" (J. ACM 2021), together with Stade's point-boundary variant (SoCG 2025), for an explicit single-tape Turing machine model. Lean proves that deciding whether a simple polygon with rational corners can be guarded by g guards is ∃ℝ-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions in each of the three variants known to be ∃ℝ-complete: point guards guarding the whole polygon (Theorem 1, also for integer corners), guards on the boundary guarding the whole polygon (the boundary-point variant of the paper's §7.2), and point guards guarding only the boundary (Stade's theorem); that ETR-INV is ∃ℝ-complete; that the guard sets of the paper's Section 5 polygon correspond exactly to the solutions of an ETR-INV instance (Theorem 54, with the range condition made explicit) and encode the solutions of any ETR formula (Theorem 55); that every real algebraic number is the x-coordinate of a guard in every optimal guard set of some polygon with rational corners (Theorem 2); and that some x-monotone polygon with integer corners can be guarded by three guards but needs four rational guards (Theorem 4). The development provides reusable material on the existential theory of the reals: formulas and their codes, the class ∃ℝ, ETR-INV and ETR-INV-REV with polynomial-time reductions from ETR, and an elementary proof of the doubly exponential solution bound that the paper cites from Schaefer and Štefankovič. It partially answers the open problem of the paper's §7.2 on the number of variables: all three art gallery problems reduce to ETR by formulas whose only variables are the 2g coordinates of the guards (the paper uses (n+g)^6 variables for n corners). Point-point and point-boundary hardness is proved through Stade's construction; the paper's own Section 5 construction is formalized for Theorems 54 and 55, with gadget visibility facts checked as kernel-evaluated certificates, and a modification of it (guard segments on shallow bays in the boundary, re-laid-out addition gadgets) gives boundary-point hardness. The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
